news.title: Pochettino to stay as USA coach until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Mauricio Pochettino has signed a contract extension to remain the head coach of the United States national team until the 2030 World Cup, U.S. football announced on Monday (August 3, 2026). The 54-year-old took over in 2024 and led the USA to the last 16 at the recent World Cup, which they co-hosted with Canada and Mexico. "It has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the men's national team program even stronger," said Argentinian Pochettino, whose coaching staff have also agreed new contracts. "The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here...”

news.title: Aleksander Ceferin wants Club World Cup boycott as he plots Gianni Infantino downfall with Nasser Al-Khelaifi talks
news.lede: Al-Khelaifi is one of Ceferin’s key allies and talkSPORT understands the UEFA President is pushing for European Football Clubs (EFC), chaired by Al-Khelaifi, to boycott the 2029 Club World Cup. However, this would require club-wide engagement with the 850+ members. Ceferin has made no secret of his own opposition to the Club World Cup, calling it a 'selfish endeavour' by Infantino back in May 2018. The inaugural 32-team edition was won by Chelsea last summer, but plans for the 2029 event remain complete up in the air.

news.title: Leandro Paredes involved in another controversial moment weeks after World Cup brawl
news.lede: Leandro Paredes has caught the headlines again for all the wrong reasons. Following the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final in which Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, USA, the defender ended up in a scuffle in which he seemingly grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before launching Gavi towards the ground. And now he’s back in hot water. On August 2, Boca Juniors travelled to Estadio Marcelo Bielsa in Rosario, Argentina, to take on Newell’s Old Boys in an Argentine Primera Division fixture.

news.title: Gianni Infantino opponents 'plotting rival World Cup competition' to 'paralyse' Fifa until he quits
news.lede: UEFA has joined forces with other confederations and threatened to set up their own version of the World Cup if disgraced Fifa supremo Gianni Infantino refuses to quit. The Swiss millionaire, 56, sensationally vowed to desperately cling onto his job after sending shockwaves through football. Infantino made shock plans to flog shares in the World Cup to private investors before being forced into a humiliating U-turn. And Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, along with Concacaf and Asian Football Confederation chiefs, is pushing for him to resign.

news.title: Socceroos on the move: Herrington headlines post-World Cup transfers
news.lede: The defender is set to become one of Australia’s most expensive players with a Premier League deal nearly done while some international teammates have already made moves. Lucas Herrington, fresh off becoming the youngest Australian to start a game at a men’s World Cup, is set to become the second-most expensive footballer in Australian history with a move to newly-promoted Premier League side Hull City. Latest reports suggest a fee of approximately £12.6m ($24.1m), with a further £4.4m ($8.4m) in add-ons, which comes in just shy of the Australian record of £15m plus £5m in add-ons ($38.3m in total) that Leicester paid Stoke City to sign Harry Souttar in 2023. It would set a new selling high-water mark for his current club, Colorado Rapids, and eclipses the decade-old record Hull set when they paid just over £10m for Ryan Mason.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: Radio presenters were 1966 World Cup heroes too | Letters
news.lede: Andrew Keeley will never forget Brian Moore and Alan Clarke’s commentary on BBC radio. Garry Richardson (England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars, 30 July) appears to make the assumption that everyone watched the 1966 World Cup final on television with Kenneth Wolstenholme’s iconic commentary. As a football-mad 10-year-old, I had the misfortune on the day of the final to be on our family summer holiday in the then sleepy village of Goathland, staying in a house with no TV. Hope rose when my dad was invited to watch the final at a neighbour’s who had one of the few TVs in the village and he asked if he could bring his children.
